item.title: Inter handed injury scare as Manuel Akanji leaves Switzerland squad early due to muscular fatigue ahead of Atalanta clash
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-SLO-SUI - AFP Inter defender Manuel Akanji has withdrawn from the Switzerland squad following an injury scare during the international break. The experienced centre-back is set to return to Italy immediately to undergo an assessment by the Nerazzurri medical staff. International break cut short Akanji has officially departed the Switzerland national team camp ahead of their upcoming Nations League fixture against Scotland on Monday night. The defender has been granted permission to return to Inter several days earlier than originally anticipated following concerns regarding his physical condition. The 31-year-old was a key figure for his country on Friday evening, completing the full 90 minutes during a hard-fought 0-0 draw away to Slovenia. According to reports from Sky Sport Italia , the decision to release Akanji from international duty was made purely on precautionary grounds. While he will miss the match against the Scots, his early return to Milan is designed to ensure he receives the necessary recovery time at his club's training base. Crucial cog in Inter's machine The news will come as a slight worry for Cristian Chivu, who has relied heavily on the former Manchester City man throughout the opening months of the 2026-27 campaign . Akanji has established himself as an almost permanent fixture in the Nerazzurri backline, starting 12 of the club's 15 competitive fixtures across all competitions. His importance to the Italian champions is underlined by his playing time, with only goalkeeper Josep Martinez and midfield engine Nicolo Barella having clocked more minutes for the side so far this season. He has started nine of Inter's 11 Serie A matches and appeared in the starting XI for three of their four Champions League ties. Focus turns to Atalanta Despite the current alarm, there is optimism within the Inter camp that Akanji - who initially joined the club on loan in September 2025 before making the move permanent in July 2026 - will be available for selection when the Nerazzurri travel to Bergamo to face Atalanta on November 22. The Nerazzurri will be eager to have the experienced defender fully fit as they continue to push hard in the title race. Inter currently sit second in the Serie A standings with 28 points, trailing league leaders Lazio by just a single point. Switzerland aim to finish dominant campaign in style Switzerland currently sit comfortably at the summit of League B, Group 1, with 13 points to their name, holding a commanding five-point advantage over second-placed Slovenia. Having already secured promotion to League A regardless of the outcome against Scotland, the Swiss will look to round off their campaign in style, having comfortably beaten the Scots 3-0 in the reverse fixture in Glasgow.

item.title: Hope cross country teams sweep regional titles for first time; women hold off Calvin by 1 point
item.description: The Hope College cross country teams made history, racing to both the men's and women's NCAA regional championships. It was the first time in program history that both teams won regionals in the same year. The Hope women won the Great Lakes Regional title with 84 points, holing off Calvin by a single point on Saturday, Nov. 14, in East Lansing, and beating the entire 35-team field. The women's regional title also was Hope's eighth, joining teams from 2021, 2017, 2015, 2012, 1987, 1986, and 1985. More: Hope men's cross country reaches national for first time in 45 years after regional title "All you have to do is look at the score and you can see it was an exciting race," Hope coach Mark Northuis said. "Our women came through. They battled, and it just shows again that it's definitely a team race and our top five really came through only 15 seconds separating our top five. That's an amazing feat and made the difference for us today." Sophomore Anna Sybenga set the pace for the Flying Dutch, breaking into the top 10 in 10th place at 22:20.0. Senior Mary England was right on her heels in 13th at 22:24.4, while freshman Ruth Miller kept the momentum rolling with a 16th-place finish in 22:29.4. Senior Olivia Ippel and sophomore Miranda Sawvel closed out Hope's scoring pack by crossing the finish line just two-tenths of a second apart. Ippel secured 22nd place in 22:34.6, immediately followed by Sawvel in 23rd at 22:34.8. "They ran great as a group," Northuis said. "We put three freshmen out there, and they performed phenomenally. Ruthie Miller just came through running third for us on this team and that's just amazing for someone who wasn't even in our Top 12 a couple weeks ago. It's been fun to watch her develop and the other ladies who are right with them." Meanwhile, the men made it back-to-back regional titles, besting the 38-team field. Hope finished with 82 points, 29 points ahead of runner-up Calvin University. Case Western Reserve University placed third with 123 points. "That was our goal all year, along with winning the conference. The guys just came through," head coach Mark Northuis said after the Flying Dutch also earned the third men's regional title in program history, joining the 2025 and 1980 teams. "Our depth again has made a big difference for us. Being able just to depend on just the steadiness of where we're at is big. They ran like they were champions. Sophomore Aiden Moore led the charge for the Flying Dutch with a fifth-place finish in 25:25.3, spearheading a trio of top-10 performances. item.title: Russia excluded from men's under-20 ice hockey worlds in Canada
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Russia's goalkeeper Andrei Vasilevskiy fails to save during the 2019 IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship Bronze medal match between Russia and Czech Republic at the Ondrej Nepela Arena. (is associated with: «Russia excluded from men's under-20 ice hockey worlds in Canada») Vít Šimánek/CTK/dpa The men's junior ice hockey world championship in Canada will take place without Russia, the sport's governing body said on Sunday. Canada, the host of the under-20 tournament, had announced that it did not plan to grant visas to Russia's team despite a recent Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling saying Russia could return to international ice hockey. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) had tried to exclude Russia on security grounds after a blanket sport ban due to the Ukraine war was phased out. "The IIHF confirms that due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian Government, the Russian U20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship," a statement said. "After carefully assessing the feasibility of alternative arrangements, the IIHF Council has determined that Canada will remain as host and the tournament will proceed from 26 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 in Edmonton and Red Deer." It is still unclear what consequences the CAS ruling will have for the men's ice hockey world championship in May in Germany. The German government may follow Canada's lead after teams and sponsors threatened a boycott. The German Ice Hockey Federation welcomed the decision on the junior worlds. "For our U20 team, the situation is now clear. That gives players and the coaching team the necessary peace for preparation, which begins in a few weeks," chairman Frank Lutz said in a statement. "The Canadian government has clearly taken a position, and many nations have shown their stance in recent weeks. We now also need to plan securely for our home world championship in May - for the teams, the fans and all partners. We therefore demand a timely clarification from the IIHF."

item.title: Everything Dan Campbell said about Aidan Hutchinson’s injury
item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Aidan Hutchinson of Detroit Lions receives medical attention after going down with an injury while celebrating getting a sack during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images We still don’t have a firm update on Aidan Hutchinson after he suffered an injury celebrating a first-down sack in the Detroit Lions’ Week 10 win over the New England Patriots . However, Lions coach Dan Campbell was asked several questions about the situation, even though he didn’t provide an exactly diagnosis. What’s the latest update on Aidan Huthcinson? Hutchinson was initially listed as questionable with a knee injury, then downgraded to out in the second half. Campbell would not offer up any additional information. “Nothing new. We’ll know more when we get back in the States,” Campbell said. “But anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate that he is, he’s a captain of ours, that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out.” Does Hutchinson’s injury put a damper on the win over the Patriots? Campbell: “Anytime you lose a player like that and you don’t know the entirety of it–but knowing Hutch for who he is. It’s like he doesn’t stay down long. It does, it hurts a little bit, but as far as this game was concerned our guys stepped up and finished. We stayed strong. This is the second time this has happened—our guys have responded in a tough situation and didn’t bat an eye. Just went back to work, and that’s not easy to do. But, no, certainly you don’t want to know that a player like that is down.” What kind of depth do the Lions have? Detroit managed to create four more sacks on the day after Hutchinson’s injury—two by rookie Derrick Moore, one from Alim McNeill, and one from DJ Wonnum. Campbell expressed confidence in the Lions’ group of pass rushers, regardless of what Hutchinson’s ultimate diagnosis is. “We like ‘em,” Campbell said. “That’s why we applied them where we did. And I know this, Derrick Moore gets better every game. The more reps he gets, he gets better. It was good to get Wonnum back today. We know what Mac [McNeill] is, Sky(ler Gill-Howard). So can Tyleik (Williams). And all those guys, even Levi (Onwuzurike), (Tyler) Lacy, they play a different flavor, but they push the pocket, they got movement. But I think the important thing is, man, we knew we had to do to get out of this game with a win. We had to play really good defense. “And I really thought the back end played outstanding. We played some stick coverage today […] We’re improving. We gotta go. We gotta go. We’ll see where Hutch is at, but we’ve gotta step up now. We need some guys to really step up—and if that is the case (with a serious Hutchinson injury), fill that role.”

item.title: USC’s Playoff Hopes Crash After Late Turnover By Jayden Maiava
item.description: Wisconsin Badgers outside linebacker Sebastian Cheeks (15) sacks USC Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava (14) during their game Oct. 24, 2026, at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wisconsin. The USC Trojans’ dream of making the College Football Playoff died on a muddy field in Bloomington, Indiana. A promising drive that looked like it would tie the game ended with quarterback Jayden Maiava throwing a fatal interception. With six minutes and 35 seconds remaining at the one-yard line, Indiana’s Isaiah Jones intercepted the pass meant for Kayden Dixon-Wyatt. That single play killed the momentum for the No. 18 ranked Trojans and handed the No. 9 Hoosiers the win. USC lost 27-13 in a game filled with self-inflicted wounds. The Trojans dropped multiple interception opportunities, missed two field goals, and committed several penalties on special teams. The New York Post reported that these mistakes were especially perplexing since USC had just finished a second bye week during which coach Lincoln Riley vowed improved performance. Instead, the team converted only two of eleven third downs and faded badly in the fourth quarter. A Season of Missed Chances The loss to Indiana was a massive blow for a team that had just beaten then-No. 2 Ohio State two weeks earlier. The loss to Indiana likely ended any real shot at the playoff. Riley now sits at a record of 1-8 against ranked opponents on the road. Grant Wilson secured the victory for the Hoosiers by connecting with Charlie Becker on a 42-yard touchdown pass as three minutes and 30 seconds were left on the clock. USC simply could not answer the call when it mattered most. Questions for Lincoln Riley The pressure is now on USC athletics director Jen Cohen to decide if Riley is the right man to lead the program. The team had put itself on the clock with “The Time Is Now” billboards around Los Angeles, yet they failed to get it done. Following kicker Caden Chittenden’s missed 27-yard field goal to the right, Riley dropped his shoulders on the sideline. That miss ended a drive that had reached Indiana’s 8-yard line, leaving the Trojans stuck at a 20-13 deficit. The errors on special teams were just the latest in a long line of mistakes. The situation got even stranger when a fan ran onto the field during a timeout and made a field goal. This bizarre moment highlighted the chaos that consumed the Trojans’ night. Riley had vowed to fix the issues after a devastating road loss to Wisconsin earlier in the season, but the same problems returned with a vengeance. The Cost of Failure When a team has as much talent as USC, losing 27-13 to a top-10 opponent is hard to explain. The Trojans (7-3 overall, 4-3 Big Ten) simply could not make the big plays needed to win. Indiana (9-1, 6-1) controlled the game when it counted. The loss raises serious questions about the future of the program in Los Angeles. Riley fell to 1-8 against ranked teams on the road, a stat that does not look good for his job security.

item.title: YSU’s Regular Season Ends with Loss – What Awaits 8-3 Penguins on Selection Sunday?
item.description: Youngstown State’s regular season came to a somewhat unceremonious close on Saturday evening. Illinois State quarterback Beckham Pellant lowered his shoulder and dove over the goal line with just nine seconds left to lift the Redbirds to a gutsy 34-33 win over the Penguins. YSU has no game next weekend so that was it, at least for the regular season. With eight wins, Beau Brungard and company will still surely be in the playoffs when the bracket gets released next Sunday. But with no further chances to build their resume, the Penguins can only wait it out and see how the chips will fall. Where… and perhaps more importantly… when will they play next? That’s the question that looms over Doug Phillips’ team right now. There is an argument to be made that they’ve done enough to avoid playing Thanksgiving weekend but also plenty to suggest that the bye week may also no longer be a possibility either. Youngstown State is 8-3 with all of their victories coming over DI teams. They have ranked wins over South Dakota, Southern Illinois, Northern Iowa and North Dakota. Two of those were Top 10 victories at the time. With all that it’s probably safe to say that they haven’t played their last home game. Whether or not it’s in the first or second round, though, will largely depend on what some of their counterparts do this next Saturday. They will want the race for the top eight seeds to remain as open as possible and thus will need some squads who are in a similar spot to lose. YSU will be rooting for the following teams this weekend: Montana State (vs. Montana) South Dakota (@ Illinois State) Northern Colorado (@ Northern Arizona) ETSU (@ Mercer) Central Arkansas (vs. Austin Peay) McNeese (vs. Lamar) If those listed teams win that keeps the 5-8 seed range quite a bit clearer for the Penguins to grab one of those spots. If that comes to pass they’d be the only group to have two weeks off before their first playoff game. Whether or not that’s a good thing is a whole different conversation. In the scenario that they do end up playing in the opening round, one would imagine that they’d receiver a higher seed in the 9-12 range. That would guarantee a home game likely against a lower conference champion from somewhere like the Ohio Valley or Pioneer League. Last year Youngstown State drew Ivy League winner Yale in the first round and it’s a game their fans would probably rather just forget. A positioning like that would set up a potential matchup against a lower-seeded bye week team if they were to advance. A second-round road trip against the likes of a Lamar, Montana, Austin Peay or Mercer is entirely possible in that case. Closing it out against Illinois State would have gone a long way in avoiding all this speculation. As of now, though, Youngstown State has left much of its postseason fate into the hands of others and the committee. There will be more football to be played nonetheless, though, and they will not have to sweat it out as a bubble team next week.

item.title: Ronaldinho turns back the clock at 46 as the Brazil legend ends his 11-year exile with a stunning Ravenna comeback
item.description: Ravenna v Forli: Serie C - Getty Images Sport Ronaldinho turned back the clock on Sunday, ending 11 years away from professional football with a sensational comeback for Ravenna at the age of 46. The Brazil legend started the Serie C derby against Forli in front of a sold-out crowd, showed flashes of his old magic and played a key part in the opening goal before being substituted at half-time. Ronaldinho starts for Ravenna in Forli derby Ronaldinho made his long-awaited comeback on Sunday, starting for Ravenna in their Serie C derby against Forli at a sold-out Stadio Bruno Benelli. The Brazilian had not played since leaving Fluminense in 2015, and came out of retirement for the third-tier club he joined as an investor in August. According to BBC Sport, he trained with his new team-mates only once, on Saturday, before the game. A team graphic had placed him on the left, but he spent most of his 45 minutes in a central role. Ronaldinho plays key part in Donati opener There were plenty of bright touches from the former Barcelona star, and he was involved in the opening goal. Ronaldinho held off a defender before playing the pass that came before the assist for Giulio Donati, who drove in a shot from outside the box. He had already carved out an earlier chance for the defender, swinging in a corner that Donati met with a header, only to see it saved. Ronaldinho was then substituted at the break, ending an outing that was streamed in several countries around the world. Dida joins Ronaldinho amid half-time frenzy The interval brought a media circus, with journalists surrounding Ronaldinho, and Dida, his former team-mate with Brazil and AC Milan, joined him on the pitch. A temporary stand, named the R10 after his famous shirt number, had been built for the fixture. In his prime, Ronaldinho won the 2002 World Cup with Brazil, the 2006 Champions League with Barcelona, and league titles with Barca and Milan. He also claimed the Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year award in 2005, and played for Paris Saint-Germain, Gremio, Flamengo, Atletico Mineiro, Fluminense and Queretaro. Will Ronaldinho play for Ravenna again? Ronaldinho scored 299 goals in his career and had hoped to reach 300 in Ravenna colours, with the plan being for him to take a penalty had the hosts been awarded one. Whether he gets another chance remains unclear, as it is not yet known if he will play again for Ravenna, who sit second in their Serie C group.

item.title: Ryan Preece Admits He Needs To Learn Heel-Toe From Shane Van Gisbergen
item.description: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images Ryan Preece knows he still has work to do on road courses. Preece told Yahoo Sports that he wants to learn how to heel-toe just like Shane Van Gisbergen. This admission shows a driver who is honest about his gaps and eager to improve his game. At Daytona International Speedway, 12 Ford Racing drivers gathered for the event on November 11. Preece partnered with Logan Sargeant for the Navy team. Robert Noaker and Austin Cindric stood out as the top contenders at the front. Ryan Blaney withdrew after a fall before the event, leading Noaker to step in. Repeated position swaps occurred between the leaders until Cindric executed a decisive pass with under five minutes left. Cindric secured victory by 0.136 seconds, while Preece claimed third and Sargeant finished fourth. Preece’s podium finish did not indicate he possessed the speed to challenge the leaders. He first had to work his way past Sargeant. By that stage, the top two had created sufficient separation to render a comeback improbable. Although the anti-lock braking system stopped the wheels from locking, Preece still needed to learn its response. Entering Daytona’s first turn, identifying the correct pressure and timing proved especially critical. His mention of heel-toe driving also warrants attention. During a downshift, this technique involves briefly blipping the throttle while braking. It aligns engine speed to maintain car balance. item.title: Move over, Peyton Manning! Josh Allen now owns another NFL record
item.description: Nov 25, 2021; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) gestures after throwing a touchdown pass in the fourth quarter against the New Orleans Saints at the Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Chuck Cook-USA TODAY Sports Josh Allen no longer has to share the top spot with Peyton Manning. The Buffalo Bills quarterback has officially moved ahead of the Pro Football Hall of Famer, becoming the NFL’s all-time leader in combined touchdowns by a quarterback through his first 10 seasons. And Allen has done it before completing his ninth year. And he did it in nine seasons. 😏 @JoshAllenQB | #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/5PKNI0B5aX — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 15, 2026 Allen entered Sunday’s game against the New York Jets tied with Manning at 322 career touchdowns. One more touchdown was all he needed to claim the record for himself. On Buffalo’s second possession of the day, Allen methodically moved the Bills down the field. After a defensive holding call gave the Bills a first and goal at the one-foot line, Allen called his own number and used the opportunity to pass Manning. Josh Allen calls his own number. 😤 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/9Fj8amAJvc — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 15, 2026 With that touchdown, Allen’s career total climbed to 323, passing the mark Manning established during his first decade with the Indianapolis Colts. But the difference between the two quarterbacks isn’t just the number of touchdowns. It’s how quickly Allen got there. Manning needed 160 regular-season games to reach 322 touchdowns. Allen matched that total in just 136 games, throwing his record-tying touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings last Monday night. That’s 24 fewer games, the equivalent of nearly a season and a half of football. Allen has also taken a different route to the record. While Manning’s touchdowns came almost exclusively through the air, Allen has been just as dangerous with his legs. His career total entering Sunday included 232 passing touchdowns, 88 rushing touchdowns, and two receiving touchdowns. Patrick Mahomes is the only other active quarterback in the top 10 who can still add to his total. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback entered Week 10 with 301 touchdowns and will spend the remainder of the season chasing Allen. But Mahomes is already in his 10th NFL season, meaning his final number will be set when the regular season ends in January. Allen, meanwhile, will have all of 2027 to keep adding to a record Mahomes will no longer be eligible to chase.

After falling to Green Bay in Week 9, New England continued its recent slide with a 35-10 loss to Detroit on Sunday. item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images The New England Patriots made a major move this offseason by trading a first-round pick for former Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver AJ Brown. The 29-year-old was expected to level up their offense and give Drake Maye an elite weapon in the passing game. However, Brown has had a quiet start in New England, recording just nine receptions for 101 yards and no touchdowns across three games. He struggled again in Sunday’s 35-10 defeat to the Detroit Lions in Munich, prompting Bill Simmons to make an unflattering comparison. Bill Simmons makes damning AJ Brown comparison after Patriots’ defeat to Lions AJ Brown’s difficult time in New England has been made worse by injuries, having already missed time this season due to knee and ankle problems. item.title: McIlroy’s Eighth Dubai Crown Proves His European Legacy Is Unshakable
item.description: Jeff Curry-Imagn Images Rory McIlroy won on Sunday and secured a legacy that now stands alongside the greats of the game. The 37-year-old Northern Irishman claimed his eighth Race to Dubai title, tying the all-time record set by Colin Montgomerie. This victory came after a nail-biting final round at the Jumeirah Golf Estates where the outcome hung in the balance until the very last holes. Per CBS Sports , the win marks his fifth straight season-long crown, a streak that shows his total command over the European circuit. McIlroy entered the final round trailing Eugenio Chacarra, who held the top spot in the standings. The Spaniard had a slight lead, but McIlroy refused to let go. A birdie on the 16th hole, described as a season-defining moment, shifted the momentum back to the world number two. This shot from 130 yards landed just a foot from the pin, a move that ultimately sealed the deal. According to Golf Monthly , the points difference between the two players was a mere 0.1 at one stage, making every single stroke matter. A Nervous Finish for the Leader Even with the title in his grasp, McIlroy admitted the pressure was real. He noted that he did not fully understand how close the race was until he reached the 16th hole. “I don’t really know what to say. … Winning eight Order of Merits was never really in my list of goals when I was growing up,” McIlroy said. The humility in his words stands out, especially given the magnitude of the achievement. He remembered watching Montgomerie as a child and now finds himself right next to him in the history books. While McIlroy took the season title, Tyrrell Hatton dominated the tournament itself. The Englishman finished at 15 under, taking a five-stroke victory over McIlroy. Hatton played with a calmness that contrasted with the tension of the Race to Dubai battle. “This is really special. I was really nervous today,” Hatton said after his win. He credited his putter for saving him all week, noting how the back nine felt like a different day than he had feared. The Margin Was Thin The margin for error was non-existent for Chacarra, who finished in a tie for third. The young Spaniard fought hard but could not make the birdie needed on the final hole to overtake McIlroy. “It was a good fight. I just came out short,” Chacarra said. He played well but acknowledged that the day required more than effort. The final numbers show McIlroy finished at 10 under par, while Chacarra closed at eight under. The prize money for the event was substantial, with Hatton taking home $3 million for his tournament victory. This win solidifies McIlroy’s status as the king of the DP World Tour. He has now won the Race to Dubai five times in a row, a feat that seems almost impossible to stop.
